situation: A student who clearly studied did poorly and is convinced they are just bad at this subject.

dims.SPEAKABILITY: Card 2's lines flow more naturally out loud, especially "that is a solvable problem — it is not a you problem," whereas Card 1's "Your brain was working hard, just on the wrong version of the task" is slightly more clinical.
dims.SPECIFICITY: Both diagnose the fixed-ability story well, but Card 2's curiosity question ("which parts felt shaky and which parts felt solid") targets the breakdown more precisely than Card 1's more open-ended "walk me through it."
dims.TIGHTNESS: Card 2 is tighter overall, though its Commitment line runs long with the "struggling means your brain is working" addition; Card 1's script is lean but its analysis sections repeat the same insight more than needed.
dims.HONESTY: Both hold the standard firmly, but Card 2 names the uncomfortable thing more sharply ("the one thing you cannot quietly agree with") while explicitly requiring redone work, edging out Card 1.
